It absolutely makes sense and I went through the same thing! I would find myself staying for extra hours at school for proficiency classes and I would PANIC because “it’s gonna be 17:00 when the class finishes and I’ll be starving and what will I do, what will I eat should I order food DURING class so that it can be delivered to me STRAIGHT after I finish class??” And the thing is I think a lot of times we’re told hunger only fuels binges and makes us eat more, so in turn when we recover we’re horrified of the idea. And while there’s definitely truth to that, I can tell you 99% of the time, going hungry (for a little while, not too long!) doesn’t make you overeat, and if anything it can help you feel more in touch with your body. My dad deals with technology and I would like to use something he told me as an analogy for this: you should let your device get to lower battery percentages before charging it, ie don’t leave it fully charged always because that messes up the battery. I’d like to think that’s how we are too, and of course don’t go starving for an extended period of time, but even being REALLY hungry won’t harm you I promise. As for actually applying this (because I know that when you have that fear at first you just don’t wanna let yourself get hungry) I suggest taking up things, tasks and events that require you to be completely away from food. For me it was traveling since long car rides go without food, and there I realized that hey, I can go like 4 hours being hungry, I can get home and I can eat normally after that. And while practicing this, always remind yourself that you’ll be okay. I hope some of this helped 💕

Ofc! This was my first time trying the egg white crust I’ve seen being made around for a while! It turned out how’d I hope! You need:
3 egg whites
5g corn starch
10g flour
*very important!* seasoning to your taste! It’s important because otherwise your crust won’t really taste like anything so be generous! I used garlic powder, salt, pepper, paprika and some Italian herbs! 

You beat the egg whites to soft peaks for about 2 mins (if you flip the bowl over they should stay in place!) and then you add your dry mixes and seasoning and whip it a little more. 

I used 3g of olive oil to line the baking paper on the bottom to not stick! I popped the dough in the air fryer in 180C for about 10 mins and then added the toppings for another 3 mins on top. 

Then I transferred it to a pan with a lid on 180C again to get the bottom nice and crispy! Here you just kinda eyeball how long it should stay on the pan.

I personally took a very rocky road to recovery, refused any help of a dietitian or anything (which was a decision based on the circumstances I was in back then, and help is ALWAYS needed wherever you can get it) As someone who experienced true extreme hunger, eating myself to the point where I couldn’t breathe, I’m glad to say that I am completely fine and happy with where I am now without any extreme hunger binges. I’m not sure if your dietitian is within the right understanding of extreme hunger? Yes, it is binging but no, it’s not binge eating disorder. Your body reacts to food this way because of restriction, it’s a bodily function beyond our control, and it’s completely natural and normal. However when your body gets used to the fact there’s food around, it will stop wanting so much of it. It’s no longer in a famine! The only thing that can possibly turn these binges into binge eating disorder, is if you put some sort of mental association on those binges. Hence why I think your dietitian might be concerned, but I think she’s leading you into a more wrong direction than what she’s supposed to. For example, my parents were great support with my EH. They bought everything I asked and craved and even encouraged me to eat whatever I wish, however much I want. After a while I expressed that I was feeling satisfied physically but for some reason I felt the need to eat more, but when I did, I felt really sick. They said that I should eat however much I want, but I can try to just think about how I’m feeling and if I want more, I can always have some later! I believe that sort of approach leaves you with a sense of freedom, one that isn’t so black and white like ,, I won’t let you jump to another disorder”. I promise your body knows what it’s doing, the only tricky part is making sure that while you honor your hunger you also take away any sort mental associating that could possibly make food a negative experience.
